The proposed rule would restrict access to medical services in cases of rape, incest, and in cases of health endangerment of the pregnant person unless the life of the pregnant person is at risk. This policy would allow the Department to willfully neglect the health of veterans and their families and deny them medically-necessary care unless they are on the brink of death. text:
===== FILE 19876__1.pdf =====
September 2, 2025 
 
Uploaded to: https://www.regulations.gov/docket/VA-2025-VHA-0073  
 
Dr. Steven L. Lieberman 
Acting Under Secretary for Health 
Department of Veterans Affairs 
810 Vermont Avenue NW 
Washington, D.C. 20420 
 
Comments on RIN 2900-AS31: Reproductive Health Services Proposed Rule 
 
Dear Dr. Lieberman: 
 
On behalf of over 1.1 million MomsRising members nationwide, we submit these comments in 
opposition to the proposed rule titled “Reproductive Health Services,” by the Department of 
Veterans Affairs (“Department” or “VA”). We oppose the proposal to reinstate the exclusion of 
all abortion services from the medical benefits package for our veterans and their families.  
 
Under the current policy, veterans and their families are guaranteed access to abortion services in 
cases of rape, incest, and in cases of health endangerment of the pregnant person. The proposed 
rule would restrict access to medical services in all these cases unless the life of the pregnant 
person is at risk. This policy would allow the Department to willfully neglect the health of 
veterans and their families and deny them medically-necessary care unless they are on the brink 
of death. This is not the standard of care we should set for our country’s heroes. 
 
This proposed rule violates a core responsibility of VA, which is to provide necessary care to 
veterans and to "promote, preserve, or restore the health" of their patients. But the VA’s proposal 
does the exact opposite: it will set a confusing standard of care where providers can only provide 
the medically-necessary treatment in certain circumstances. Out of fear of retaliation, service 
providers may offer a false prognosis, and the consequences could be fatal. Our veterans fought 
for our fundamental freedoms. To strip them of their rights - including the ability to live a safe 
and healthy life - is an insult to all who have served.  
 
It is important to note that 6 in 10 women who access abortion are already moms. Additionally, 
this proposal will have a particularly harmful impact on women veterans of color. As you know 
Black women are disproportionately represented in the US military and in the veteran 
population. Black women are three times more likely to experience a pregnancy-related death 
than white women and are more likely to experience preventable maternal death compared with 
white women. Restrictions on abortion coverage - the effects of which fall hardest on people who 
already face unequal access to health care, including Black women - interfere with a person’s 
right to make decisions about their health and well-being.  
 
We all deserve the freedom to control our own bodies, safely care for our families, and live with 
dignity. Below are comments from our MomsRising members who share the impact of the 
proposed policy reversal by the Department: 
 

The young women of the Armed Forces get raped everyday and nothing is done about it. I 
was one of them years ago, the only reason I did not get pregnant was because I was on 
birth control. I had to have a hysterectomy for taking them too long. Don't assume we are 
safe in the Armed Forces, women have to fight two battles: 1) being a woman and 2) not 
being raped. - Barbara, Armed Forces Veteran, Georgia 
 
Cutting abortion care when military sexual assault is rampant in these difficult times 
would be like throwing the baby out with the bathwater. Kindly keep abortion services for 
my veteran sisters. - Jim, US Navy, Vietnam Veteran, California 
 
The Department should be thanking our veterans by offering our heroes and their families the 
full spectrum of care available – which includes access to abortions. Leaving veterans who have 
been sexually assaulted, veterans who would suffer severe health consequences for carrying a 
pregnancy to term, or any veteran in need of an abortion without the care they need is not how 
we should honor their service. For these reasons, we strongly oppose the proposed rule to restrict 
reproductive healthcare for our veterans.  
 
Sincerely,  
 
Tina Sherman 
National Director for Maternal Justice 
MomsRising Together & MomsRising Education Fund 
 
Gina Arias, RN, MPH 
Campaign Director for Maternal Mental Health 
MomsRising Together & MomsRising Education Fund
